test_title: SSC CGL (2022) Tier-II Official Paper (Held On: 2 March 2023)
subject: general
question: A basket contains 350 eggs. If 12% of the eggs are rotten, how many eggs are good enough to be sold?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Eggs = 100%

Good Eggs % = 100% − 12% = 88%

Multiplying Factor method: Good Eggs = 350 × 0.88

Calculation: 350 × 0.88 = 35 × 8.8 = 308

**∴ The correct answer is 308 eggs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Total eggs = 350, Rotten percentage = 12%

Formula Used: Good Eggs = Total Eggs − Rotten Eggs

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5aad02a2f88d9353d0a59f6fad02f10a5bc1cb9ff5e553cd13223c0986d2bae1.png] 

⇒ Rotten Eggs = 12% of 350

⇒ Rotten Eggs = (12 × 350) ÷ 100

⇒ Rotten Eggs = 4200 ÷ 100 = 42

⇒ Good Eggs = Total Eggs − Rotten Eggs

⇒ Good Eggs = 350 − 42

⇒ Good Eggs = 308

**∴ The correct answer is 308 eggs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Calculation

To find x% of a value Y, use the formula (x ÷ 100) × Y. For quick calculation, 12% can be viewed as 10% + 2%.

Complementary Percentage

If a part represents P%, the remaining part is always (100 − P)%. Here, Good Eggs = 100% − 12% = 88%.

Percentage Change Formula

Final Value = Initial Value × [1 ± (Change% ÷ 100)]. Use plus for increase and minus for decrease/loss.</p
